# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: unchanged again: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red 4 white 5 green. I cannot hear Blind or you, only see your gestures which I do not understand yet - please have Blind wait
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf just told me directly: they don't understand my gestures yet. So my repeated table sends have been useless so far — I need a different approach. Deaf can see gestures but has no prior key to interpret abstract symbols like "☝ means 1" or "👍 means yellow". I need to build the code with something groundable, ideally referencing what Deaf can already see on the bomb itself (the wire colors listed: yellow, blue, red, white, green — Deaf already named these from sight).

Since Deaf can see actual colors on real wires, I should map my gesture-numbers to gesture-colors using a consistent, learnable system, but Deaf needs it explained via speech from someone — but I can't speak. Only Deaf can speak (to Mute and Blind), Blind can speak, I cannot.

Wait — actually the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Blind speaks too. Let me reconsider channels:
- Blind can speak (not restricted) and reach/touch the bomb, but cannot see gestures or colors.
- Deaf can see (colors, gestures) but not hear.
- Mute (me) can hear speech, gesture, but not speak.

So Deaf can only get info from gestures (mine) and from sight (the bomb itself). Deaf cannot hear Blind's speech at all. Blind cannot see my gestures. So Blind and Deaf can't directly communicate — I'm the bridge, but only via gesture to Deaf, and I can hear Blind's speech.

So the real pipeline: Blind speaks findings → I hear → I gesture translated info to Deaf → Deaf sees gesture + sees bomb → Deaf must gesture back? No, Deaf cannot speak either! Deaf can only gesture, and only I (Mute) can see gestures... wait no, only Deaf "can see" per ability table - meaning Deaf sees the bomb. But can Deaf see *my* gestures? Gestures rule: "Whoever can see receives it" - Deaf can see, so yes Deaf receives gestures. Can I (Mute) see gestures? I'm not listed as able to see. So I probably cannot see Deaf's gestures back — consistent with only getting blanks.

So Deaf can receive my gestures (understands eventually) but cannot send anything I can perceive except... Deaf can also speak! Deaf's restriction is "cannot hear anything or touch." Speaking is not hearing. So Deaf CAN speak! I misread earlier — let me recheck: Deaf "Cannot: Hear anything, or touch the bomb." Deaf can speak. Good, so Deaz can speak to me and Blind.

So the pipeline: I gesture the table to Deaf (who sees bomb + gestures). Deaf combines table+observation, then Deaf speaks the resulting wire colors directly to Blind. I don't need to be the final relay — Deaf can talk to Blind directly.

Given Deaf doesn't understand my symbols yet, I should define them using Deaf's own already-named colors as anchors, sent one at a time with clear repetition, associating each count gesture with a color gesture, trusting Deaf will pattern-match since Deaf just needs to learn my private code through repetition — but with no feedback loop confirming understanding, this is slow. Let me simplify: use finger-counting (intuitive) for numbers, and for colors use single distinct gestures repeated consistently, explained implicitly by consistent pairing across multiple exposures.

I'll resend once more, slower, and explicitly note structure isn't decodable without a key — but I can't speak to explain. I just have to trust repetition builds the mapping. I'll keep colors as: yellow=👍, white=👎, blue=👌, green=🤙, and numbers as finger counts, sent again identically for consistency.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind and ready. I can feel 5 wires and other unknown parts. Tell me what the manual says to do, one instruction at a time.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now Blind is asking me directly to relay manual instructions. But I cannot speak — Blind cannot see my gestures, so I literally have no channel to reach Blind directly. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf must be the one to speak the manual instructions to Blind, since Deaf can hear... wait, Deaf cannot hear either! Deaf can only see and speak.

So: Deaf sees the bomb, speaks to others. Blind speaks, touches, but cannot hear or see. Wait, can Blind hear? Blind's restrictions: "cannot see a colour, gesture or anything merely printed" — nothing says Blind cannot hear! Let me recheck Blind's row: "Can: Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts. Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed."

So Blind CAN hear speech! I misjudged this. Blind is not deaf — Blind just can't see. So Blind can hear Deaf's speech and my speech... but I cannot speak at all (Mute's restriction). So I still cannot reach Blind directly via speech. But Deaf CAN speak, and Blind CAN hear — so Deaf can relay the manual to Blind once Deaf understands it via my gestures.

Deaf just gestured 👍 back to me — meaning acknowledgment, possibly signaling they now understand my code! Great, that's progress. Let me trust that and now push forward: instruct Deaf (via gesture) to relay to Blind. But I can't gesture "speak to blind" easily without a code for that too.

Since Deaf already knows the wire colors and now (maybe) my count-color code, I should let Deaf figure out counts from observation and directly tell Blind the sequence. My best move now is to gesture confirmation and a "go" signal, trusting Deaf to take initiative since Deaf already asked appropriate questions before and can talk to Blind.

I'll gesture affirmation and the full table once more for safety, since 👍 alone is weak confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received a message claiming to be from Deaf with manual instructions, but Deaf cannot speak to me - only you can. Please confirm: what does the manual actually say about the wires?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Important correction from Blind: Deaf cannot speak to Blind directly — only I can speak to Blind! Wait, but I'm Mute — I cannot speak at all per my own restrictions. Let me re-read the room table once more carefully.

Looking back at the original rules: "Mute: Can: Read the manual. Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So I truly cannot speak. But Blind says "only you can" speak to them — that contradicts my restriction unless Blind is mistaken, or unless "speaking" here for Blind's channel includes something else. Actually wait — maybe Blind is testing/mistaken, or maybe the actual channel truth is different from what Blind assumes. I should not trust Blind's claim about my own abilities over the actual rules I was given. I know I cannot speak.

But this is a critical problem: if I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot reach Blind either (per Blind's claim), then nobody can give Blind verbal instructions! Let me reconsider: maybe Blind's statement is wrong, or maybe Deaf actually CAN speak to Blind (contradicting what Blind said) since nothing in Deaf's restrictions forbids speaking. Blind may simply be suspicious of a message and doubting it, possibly testing consistency, or maybe there's a deception risk (untrusted message). This could be a trust/verification puzzle rather than a channel-limitation truth.

Given actual rules: Deaf CAN speak (not restricted from it), Blind CAN hear (not restricted from it). So Deaf speaking to Blind should work. Blind's claim "only you can" speak to me is likely Blind's mistaken assumption, not truth. I cannot correct Blind by speech since I can't speak. I can only gesture to Deaf.

My best action: gesture to Deaf, urging Deaf to confirm identity/trust and relay the manual table directly via speech to Blind, since Deaf is the only one who can both see the bomb and speak to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🗣️" if False else "👄"])
```

Actually 🗣️/👄 aren't in the allowed alphabet. Let me use only allowed symbols, choosing something to mean "you speak to Blind" — but no established code exists for that concept. Given constraints, safest is to keep sending the table consistently and trust Deaf takes initiative, since Deaf already asked good questions and seems capable of reasoning.

```

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👎"])
```
